candidate.answerReason: The specified diagonal represents fifty miles. It divides the sixty-degree rhombus into two equilateral triangles of side fifty, whose total area is \(1250\sqrt3\).

methods.label: Convert the diagonal and find two triangle areas
methods.explanation:
First convert the given diagonal to its actual length. Since \(\tfrac32\) inches represents four hundred miles, the diagonal represents
\[
\frac3{16}\div\frac32\times400
=\frac18\times400=50\text{ miles}.
\]

Label the actual rhombus \(ABCD\), with \(\angle DAB=60^\circ\). The diagonal opposite this angle is \(BD\), so \(BD=50\). Triangle \(ABD\) has \(AB=AD\) and an included angle of \(60^\circ\); hence it is equilateral. Thus every side of the rhombus is fifty miles. Triangle \(BCD\) also has all three sides equal to fifty, so it too is equilateral.

An altitude in either equilateral triangle bisects its fifty-mile base. By Pythagoras, its height is
\[
h=\sqrt{50^2-25^2}=25\sqrt3\text{ miles}.
\]
The diagonal divides the rhombus into these two triangles, so its area is
\[
2\left(\frac12\cdot50\cdot25\sqrt3\right)
=\boxed{1250\sqrt3\text{ square miles}},
\]
choice E.
